boundary: a bound between two PLANES of one AVBuffer, as av_frame_get_buffer carves them
title: Upstream FFmpeg spatial defects that leave a frame PLANE while staying inside the frame's single allocation
note: The third FFmpeg corpus and the one the inventory's nested-spatial cell needed. pool-repros holds storage an AVBufferPool handed out and took back (temporal); subobject-repros holds a bound between two MEMBERS of one av_malloc (spatial, NOT nested, because av_refstruct_alloc_ext is called directly); this one holds a bound between two PLANES of one AVBuffer, which is spatial AND nested. That every plane comes from a single buffer is measured rather than assumed: a YUVA420P frame reports buf[1] == NULL with 1024 bytes of slack after the alpha plane inside that one buffer, so a read leaving the plane stays inside the allocation exactly as a wmem chunk overread stays inside its block. ASan is SILENT here and reports the memcached plain-heap row; the two readings side by side are the project's axis, measured rather than argued. The declared port is the app port rather than buffer-pool: buffer-pool compiles only libavutil/buffer.c and refstruct.c, while this case needs frame.c, imgutils.c and pixdesc.c, so the app port (whole libavutil) is the only one that could host a domain build of it. Today the corpus is native-only.
